intent: Extract linux_configuration/periodic_background/hosts/ into its own public repo (github.com/kuhyx/hosts-blocker, cloned at ~/hosts-blocker), clearing 5 of the 46 remaining directory-depth violations without disturbing the live hosts blocker or its guards.
scope: REWRITTEN callers: check_and_enable_services.sh, setup_periodic_system.sh, features/setup_dns_blocker.sh, fixes/migrate_hosts_guard_to_guard_lib.sh, install_core_system.sh, fresh-install/main.sh
NON-GOAL: removing --warn from the depth hook — only valid once BOTH units are out
NON-GOAL: reformatting the guard plugins with shfmt
changes: git filter-repo across ALL FOUR historical roots (hosts/, linux_configuration/hosts/, linux_configuration/scripts/periodic_background/hosts/, linux_configuration/periodic_background/hosts/) with matching --path-rename rules. Filtering on the current path alone would have preserved 1 commit instead of 51 — the flatten had moved the unit recently, so a naive single --path silently truncates the history to the flatten commit.

No source file was modified during extraction: all 15 files are byte-identical to the monorepo copies (verified with diff -r). install.sh already resolved its lib/ via BASH_SOURCE and needed no rewrite.

Added linux_configuration/lib/extracted_repos.sh: resolves an extracted repo's checkout via SUDO_USER's passwd entry (NOT $HOME, which is /root under sudo), supports a <NAME>_DIR override, and fails loudly with a clone instruction when absent.
Reused the existing REAL_HOME resolution already present in check_and_enable_services.sh for screen-locker rather than sourcing a second resolver into it.
fresh-install/main.sh uses "$HOME/hosts-blocker/install.sh" because it runs from ~/linux-configuration (a different repo) and is not sudo-re-exec'd at that point.

The new repo ships NO shfmt hook, deliberately: guard/plugins/*.sh are space-indented and unformatted in the monorepo too (its git hook shfmt's only STAGED files), and their installed copies under /usr/local/share/guard-lib-plugins/ are byte-identical by md5. An shfmt hook would rewrite both on first commit and break that identity.

The live hosts blocker was NOT re-installed as part of this change; /etc/hosts and its guards are untouched and still enforced from their installed copies.
